On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 08:35 AM rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Anika — sorry to hear this. I’m escalating immediately.

Investigating now. Early hypothesis: NAT port (ephemeral) exhaustion on Nebula's egress gateway or our egress path (SNAT) causing connection failures and triggering retries. Symptoms match: many short-lived outbound connections, lots of TIME_WAIT, and 429/5xx from our edge when client connections fail mid-stream.

What I’ve done so far:
- Checked cluster-side agent logs for increased 5xx triggers — saw increased upstream timeouts around 07:58–08:06 UTC.
- Looked at our LB metrics: spike in connection attempts and concurrent connections; backend worker processes queuing.
- Asked infra to check iptables/conntrack and NAT tables on peer gateways.

Immediate mitigations to propose (we can run these as temporary while we diagnose):
1) Ask Nebula Ops to increase conntrack/nat table size and ephemeral port range on their NAT gateway (temporary).
2) Route traffic for Nebula through alternate egress (we can bring up cross-region fallback) — will add latency but reduce timeouts.
3) Deploy a short-lived rate-limiter at our ingress to smooth bursty retries (prevent retry storm).
4) If acceptable, failover Nebula to a hosted fallback model for a short window (requires exec approval for credits).

Need:
- Nebula pcap/pcap snippet (they said they can share)
- Confirmation whether their firewall/NAT device has any rate-limiting or connection-tracking caps.

I’ll continue debugging and post kernel/conntrack metrics soon.

-Stephanie
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Stephanie — attaching PCAP snippet and CloudWatch traces. The peer NAT is an AWS-managed NAT Gateway in our VPC; we can change some config but don't control the appliance itself beyond scaling. We are seeing source port reuse and apparent exhaustion around 07:59 UTC. Our Load Balancer also logged a retry burst when backends returned 502/504 intermittently.

Attachments: pcap-snippet.pcap, cloudwatch-graphs.png

We can temporarily scale the NAT gateway (increase allocation) and open a ticket with AWS, but we'd prefer Redwood to provide a quicker mitigation because the business impact is material — trading sessions are failing. What’s the ETA on a hosted fallback?

- Anika

- Stephanie: continue root cause; capture kernel conntrack stats and provide a short RCA with mitigation timeline by EOD.
- Tessa / CS: keep Anika informed and confirm stakeholder communication cadence; offer credits and hosted fallback as an option.

Customer asks: ETA on hosted fallback + an immediate mitigation we can apply on our side (they can scale NAT but need AWS ticket).
